text:
lina (product): quick sync — netops wants a concrete rollforward/upgrade path for private distro when customers opt for customer-managed networking. decision needed by EOD Fri. two options: require a static egress IP per-tenant, or support a relay fallback + short rotation windows. thoughts?
rahul (netops): +1 on getting this scoped. static egress IP is simplest for peering/ACLs but painful for fleets that expect ephemeral ips. relay adds ops cost but avoids customer churn.
jess (field): most pilot customers prefer not to change their infra. they can add a NAT IP but ask for minimal handholding from us. also many customers on prem use NAT pools that rotate every 24h.
mike (eng): technical take: we can support both, toggled by installer flag. operator shim preserves SNAT mapping if configured; otherwise route traffic via relay service in our VPC. relay has latency/cost hit but is easier on onboarding.
lina (product): sounds like flexibility is key. for launch we should support both but ship with a conservative default. do we have a minimal config snippet we can show to customers?
mike (eng): yes — sample config below we can include in docs:

```
# installer values.yaml
network:
  mode: customer-managed # customer-managed | redwood-relay
  egress_policy: preserve-ip # preserve-ip | relay
  egress:
    static_ip: 198.51.100.4 # optional, required if preserve-ip
```

rahul (netops): note: preserve-ip requires either a customer route to our node IPs or BGP advertisement. if customers can't do that we fallback to relay. need runbook for verifying SNAT mappings.
jess (field): add to runbook: "how to test egress preservation" steps for NetOps teams. they want a 5-min checklist.
mike (eng): putting a quick smoke test for egress in the installer:

```
# smoke test (runs post-install)
curl -sS https://ifconfig.redwood.example/verify?expected=198.51.100.4
# returns JSON {"observed": "198.51.100.4"}
```

lina (product): good. launch criteria proposal (draft):
- docs: networking handshake + minimal installer examples (PR ready)
- runbook: netops checklist + troubleshooting steps
- installer: supports both modes, smoke test passes
- upgrade path: can rollforward in <30m and has automated rollback
- field validation: 2 reference customers tested (one preserve-ip, one relay)

rahul (netops): add: network acceptance test that asserts no tenant ejection after upgrade. also require packet-capture snippets for debug.
mike (eng): implementation note: operator shim will tag flows with tenant-id in conntrack for easier mapping during rolling upgrades. low-risk but needs QA.
jess (field): can we add a small FAQ about why we might ask for a static IP? customers keep asking about "why me". short blurb saves time.
lina (product): yep. i'll draft the FAQ. who owns the runbook? @rahul?
rahul (netops): i'll own runbook + acceptance test. will pair with @mike on the smoke tests.
mike (eng): i'll take installer + operator shim. estimate: 2 sprint cycle to have both modes in CI.
jess (field): i'll arrange the two customer pilots for validation next week.
lina (product): next steps / action items:
- lina: draft FAQ + handshake doc (today)
- rahul: runbook skeleton + acceptance test (by Thu)
- mike: PR for installer flags + smoke test (start tomorrow)
- jess: schedule pilots (by Mon)

kube-bot: deploy scheduled -> env=staging, job=network-smoke v1.2.3 :rocket:

lina (product): thanks everyone :thumbsup: will reconvene Fri 10am to lock decision. if anyone wants to add edge cases (e.g., double-NAT, egress IP pools), drop them here.
rahul (netops): edge case: ISPs that rewrite source IPs on egress (we've seen this). will document detection steps.
mike (eng): edge case: cluster upgrades that rotate node IPs — operator shim needs to persist expected SNAT mapping across node churn.
jess (field): customer ask: ability to opt into relay temporarily during maintenance windows without reinstall. can we support a flip flag?
mike (eng): yes — we'll add runtime toggle to the control plane config: `network.egress_policy` can be changed and triggers a short reconciliation.
lina (product): perfect. capturing this in the decision doc. thanks :eyes:
